FN-AKG5SSQ-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 137
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development Sponsor: Senator Garlan Gudger
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/21/2024
Senate Bill 137 as introduced would terminate the existing seven-member Alabama Board of Massage
Therapy on June 1, 2024 and transfer all rights, duties, records, and property to the newly created
nine-member Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board. This will increase the new board's
obligations by an estimated minimum of $1,300 annually for per diem and travel expenses of the
additional board members to attend biannual meetings for license renewal.
This bill would (1) require the Alabama Board of Massage Therapy Fund to be renamed the Alabama
Massage Therapy Licensing Board Fund; and (2) provide that all administrative rules of the former
board shall remain in effect as rules of the new board until amended or repealed.
This bill provides for the continuance of the Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board until October
1, 2025 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law.

FN-AKG5SSQ-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 137
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development Sponsor: Senator Garlan Gudger
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/22/2024
Senate Bill 137 as reported by the Committee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
would terminate the existing Alabama Board of Massage Therapy on June 1, 2024 and transfer all
rights, duties, records, and property to the newly created Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board.
This bill would increase board membership by two additional members and would require the board to
meet quarterly (rather than biannually) which will increase the new board's obligations by an estimated
minimum of $7,300 annually for per diem and travel expenses of the additional board members to attend
meetings for license renewal. The provisions of this bill would further increase the obligations of the
new board by an undetermined amount for any requests of criminal history background checks of certain
licensees made through the district attorneys of the circuits where the licensees are located. This bill
would also (1) require the Alabama Board of Massage Therapy Fund to be renamed the Alabama
Massage Therapy Licensing Board Fund; and (2) provide that all administrative rules of the former
board shall remain in effect as rules of the new board until amended or repealed.
This bill would also increase the obligations of the Office of the Secretary of State, as the executive
director of the board, to perform all of the administrative functions of the board. However, any
increased obligations could be offset wholly or partly by board receipts.
This bill provides for the continuance of the Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board until October
1, 2026 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law.

FN-AKG5SSQ-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 137
Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions Sponsor: Senator Garlan Gudger
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/19/2024
Senate Bill 137 as passed the Senate would terminate the existing seven-member Alabama Board of
Massage Therapy on June 1, 2024 and transfer all rights, duties, records, and property to the
nine-member Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board created by this bill. This bill would increase
the new board's obligations by an estimated minimum of $1,300 annually for per diem and travel
expenses of the additional board members to attend biannual meetings for license renewal.
This bill would also: (1) require the Alabama Board of Massage Therapy Fund to be renamed the
Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board Fund; (2) provide for the same amount or limits on fees and
fines as provided by current law; and (3) provide that all administrative rules of the former board shall
remain in effect as rules of the new board until amended or repealed.
This bill would provide for the continuance of the Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board until
October 1, 2026 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law.

FN-AKG5SSQ-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 137
Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions Sponsor: Senator Garlan Gudger
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/24/2024
Senate Bill 137 as reported by the Committee on Boards, Agencies and Commissions would create the
Office of Occupational and Professional Licensing within the Department of Labor to
serve as a centralized entity providing leadership, support, and oversight to certain professional
or occupational licensing boards operating within the state. This would increase the obligations
of the Department of Labor to hire an executive director, deputy directors, and any other
administrative staff the director deems necessary, and would decrease the financial obligations
of such boards from personnel costs for currently employed executive directors and other staff
and/or from costs for contracted management services. This bill would also streamline board
member compensation by establishing a flat rate per diem of $100 per day, which would
increase or decrease the obligations of the Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the
difference in the new flat rate and the amounts paid under existing law.
In addition, this bill would: (1) redirect any funds received by the individual boards from their current
funds in the State Treasury to the newly created Occupational and Professional Licensing Fund in the
State Treasury; and (3) require the executive director to establish fees for the operation of the boards,
which could increase or decrease receipts to the Occupational and Professional Licensing Fund by an
undetermined amount dependent upon the difference in each board's current fee structure under
current law and the fee structure set by the executive director under the provisions of this bill.
This bill further would reconstitute the existing seven-member Alabama Board of Massage Therapy to
the nine-member Alabama Massage Therapy Licensing Board on June 1, 2024 and temporarily provide
that the Board of Nursing assume all duties and functions of the board until the establishment of the
Office of Occupational and Professional Licensing on or before November 1, 2024.
This bill would also: (1) repeal the Alabama Board of Massage Therapy Fund and provide that all
receipts of the Board be deposited into the Occupational and Professional Licensing Fund, created by
